groups.title: Section A · 第 1 篇 · 1–4 题
groups.material:
W: I must say, I love our canteen! It's such a great meeting point!
M: Yeah, it really is, both for students and teachers. Shame about the food.
W: What do you mean? I think the food is fine.
M: I would say the food is just OK, but the prices are absurd. Don't you agree?
W: I don't, actually. I personally think they're perfectly appropriate. If it's overpriced, why does it get so frantically busy at lunchtimes?
M: Hmm, you make a good point. I guess a lot of it is good value, maybe even most of it. However, don't you think 6 bucks for a slice of apple crumble is beyond most students' budgets?
W: Um, yes, desserts are overpriced. I'll give you that. To be honest, I've forgotten about those, as I never eat them. I never really crave sweet things or any fancy delicacies. What I always go for is their scrambled eggs. They have such a great variety.
M: Yeah, those are good. They also come out really fast. Actually, that's one of the best things about the canteen — the speed. If I fancy something more substantial than a sandwich, but I don't have much time for lunch, the university canteen is always a good option. The kitchen staff work at such a brisk pace. They really deserve to be complimented for it.
W: Totally, and it's such a great environment too. Like the entire building is beautiful.
M: It is very nice.
W: The massive glass windows make all the difference. I think they're so cool. Apparently, they did a massive renovation a few years ago. It cost them a pretty penny.
M: Yeah, I'm not surprised. It's a very versatile space, suitable both for eating and relaxing.
W: And for working.
M: You're right, working too. I've used my laptop there once or twice. And there's always a group project or meeting going on at the far end.

groups.title: Section A · 第 2 篇 · 5–8 题
groups.material:
W: Hi, Tony, today we're talking about how managers can get along better with young people at work. We often hear young people today have a poor work ethic. That's not really justified though, is it?
M: Not really. In reality, young people of this age group are as varied and multifaceted as any other generation.
W: Yeah, but if you are struggling to work with young people in your workspace, what can you do?
M: Well, it's essential to connect with them to learn about their values. It's also really important to recognize the way young people want to balance their work life with their personal life.
W: So they generally don't want to defer happiness in return for career advancement?
M: Absolutely. They are not willing to sacrifice their personal lives for their work lives and this leads people to equate that with an unwillingness to work hard.
W: Right. But that couldn't be further from the truth, could it?
M: Young people will work extremely hard during their defined work hours, but they expect to have their time off, like weekends and nights free from work.
W: So how should managers go about assessing young people's productivity?
M: Generally, young people believe their productivity should not be measured by the number of hours they work, since someone can work for eight hours and accomplish next to nothing of significance for the company. Instead, young people measure their productivity levels by the quality of the work they perform.
W: But we often hear that young people want to feel more than just being a part of a big machine. Such a perspective can be hard to discredit, can't it?
M: It's important to legitimize their work. Young workers want to work on projects that matter to themselves, the company or the world at large. They must feel the need to stay working at a company whose values align with their own.
W: Thanks for your advice.

groups.title: Section B · 第 1 篇 · 9–11 题
groups.material:
Many restaurants are trying to persuade customers to eat more sustainably, moving away from environmentally unfriendly meat towards greener dishes. Although it sounds counter-intuitive, restaurants which include specific vegetarian sections on their menus may be unintentionally encouraging customers to eat meat, a new study suggests.
Behavioral scientist Linda Bacon, one of the study's authors, said, "Restaurants can have a positive impact on the environment by encouraging their customers to choose more plant-based food and less meat. However, our findings suggest that while certain restaurant menu designs can encourage some consumers to make pro-environmental food choices, they can have the opposite effect on others." The study involved 750 people, half of whom frequently ate vegetarian food and half of whom rarely ate it. No vegetarians were included. They were given different menus and asked to choose a meal as if they were eating out with friends. Placing vegetarian dishes in a separate section did not have a significant effect on the choices made by infrequent vegetarian food eaters. But it did have a notable effect on the frequent eaters, lowering their chance of picking a vegetarian option by 65%. The researchers also discovered that presenting a vegetarian dish as the chef's recommendation, or including a more appealing description of a non-meat meal, leads to a greater proportion of infrequent vegetarian eaters choosing a vegetarian option. But again, these altered menu designs backfired with those who ate vegetarian food more frequently, leading them to be less likely to choose a vegetarian dish.

groups.title: Section B · 第 2 篇 · 12–15 题
groups.material:
Nottingham Trent University and the Chinese Academy of Sciences have been trying to find a way to prevent deadly outdoor air pollution from penetrating indoors. They found that if pollution is frozen to around –18 ℃ in a condensing tube, the particles gather together and fall to the bottom, allowing fresh, clean air to pass through. Their method was able to remove 99% of pollutants. It is hoped that the work could pave the way for simple modification of air conditioning units so that they can also clean polluted indoor air.
Outdoor air pollution in cities is a global problem, whether it be haze plaguing Calcutta or poor air impacting the health of children in London schools. While there are some existing technologies to purify indoor air, they can be inefficient, expensive or produce harmful by-products. When outdoor air quality is poor, people tend to spend even more time indoors. But outdoor pollution also leads to indoor pollution, and people still suffer. It is estimated that pollution is linked to over 40,000 early deaths in Britain each year. Professor Gang Pan of the Chinese Academy of Sciences said, "We have shown in our experiments that simply by circulating polluted air through a small freezing chamber, we can remove most of the fine particles and gas pollutants. Our study makes it possible to add an air cleaner option to household appliances in areas which might experience extremely poor air conditions. By controlling indoor air pollution and improving air quality in this way, this work could be greatly beneficial to public health."

groups.title: Section C · 第 1 篇 · 16–18 题
groups.material:
Research recently carried out by my team suggests that fish may be self-aware. A certain species of fish recently passed the well-known mirror test.
This is a test that demonstrates self-recognition in animals. Only a few animals, such as humans, apes, dolphins and some birds, can recognize themselves in a mirror. And only these animals, capable of self-recognition, will attempt to remove marks placed on their skin after noticing them in the reflection. This ability suggests a level of higher intelligence and awareness. This is not shown by children until around 18 months. Until now, no fish has demonstrated the ability. But our experiments show the fish in question will scrape up against hard surfaces to remove marks placed on its body by our researchers after viewing itself in a mirror. The behaviors we observe leave little doubt that this fish behaviorally fulfills all criteria of the mirror test as originally laid out. The fish in our study never attempted to remove the marks when no mirror was present or when the marks were just placed on the mirror. Unmarked fish also did not attempt to remove marks from themselves when interacting with a marked fish on the other side of a window. These results show either that fish are self-aware or that the mirror test, which is considered to be the gold standard test used to denote higher intelligence, may be flawed.
What is less clear is whether these behaviors should be considered as evidence that fish are self-aware, even though in the past these same behaviors have been interpreted as self-awareness in so many other animals. Depending on your position, you might reject the interpretation that these behaviors in a fish satisfy passing the test at all. But on what objective basis can you do this when the behaviors they show are so functionally similar to those of other species that have passed the test?
Results from our research raise more questions than answers. What if self-awareness develops like an onion, building layer upon layer rather than appearing all at once? Perhaps in order to explore self-awareness further, we should stop looking at responses to the mirror as a decisive test. Only with a richer theory of the self and a larger test battery will we be able to determine all of the various levels of self-awareness, including where exactly fish fit in.

groups.title: Section C · 第 2 篇 · 19–21 题
groups.material:
Reading with a young child is important. But does it matter whether you read from an electronic book or traditional print? As any parent knows, small children are generally keen on screens. So the finding from a new study that very young children enjoy electronic books more than printed picture books may not come as a huge surprise — but the following additional findings might: both parents and children behaved differently when reading electronic versus printed picture books. And the children who read the electronic books learned more.
Previous studies of young children have suggested that electronic books, which incorporate extra features such as dictionaries and images that depict story events, may have advantages over print. In fact, multiple studies have found that electronic books support story comprehension and vocabulary gains beyond what is provided by printed books. But there's also work suggesting that children sometimes invest less mental effort in learning from electronic books, and that parents talk less about content when sharing such books.
The study we're looking at today aims to give us a better understanding of how good electronic books are for young children. For this study, researchers videoed children aged 17 to 26 months reading with one of their parents. Each parent-child pair was randomly assigned to read either two educational electronic books or two printed books with the same content. While the parent read the words in the printed books aloud, the electronic books had audio of voice actors reading the text.
The researchers found that parents who read the printed books pointed more frequently to pages than parents who read the electronic books. But the opposite was true for the children. Children who read the electronic books also commented more on the content and learned more new words than the children who read printed books.
This greater learning is ascribed to greater engagement with the electronic books. It's important to note that the electronic books in the study were simple. While they included background music, animation and sound effects, there were no other extra features.
It's also important to note that there's research on older children, finding that electronic books don't always bolster learning. Parents and educators need to beware. Extra features in electronic books may increase children's participation with them; however, if these features don't draw attention to the educational content, they may not serve as a supportive feature.

groups.title: Section C · 第 3 篇 · 22–25 题
groups.material:
Let me be honest with you. If you're living your life full of regrets, you're wasting your time. Why would you go through life regretting the very decisions that made you who you are today? There are plenty of unfavorable decisions we've made, but does that mean we should regret them? No!
I've had many moments where I sit and think about all the things I wish I could have done differently. However, just because things could be different, it doesn't necessarily mean they would be better. You don't have to continually be thinking of all your past decisions and whether or not you made the right one. You can't go back and change anything, so what's the point in worrying about it?
Every single decision you've ever made, positive or negative, has made you the person you are today. We want to go back and change parts of our past, but what would be the benefit of that? We would have lost the valuable knowledge from the lessons we learned.
There are reasons you make the choices you do, and that tells us about who you are. So when it comes to any decision in life, be unapologetically yourself. Because at the end of the day, it was you who made that decision.
With less time spent focused on regrets, you'll finally have time to focus on the more essential things in life. In any situation, you grow more as a person with every decision you make. Life is full of lessons to learn, so we can't let regret stop us from moving forward.
We don't know if we've made the right or wrong choice until after it's already been made, so it can be easy to start regretting your decision. But if the decision has already been made, what's the purpose of dwelling on it? There isn't one. All you can do is move forward. You can't let yourself sit there and worry about every past choice. We aren't all perfect.
Whenever you make a decision, there will always be a possibility for regret later, but that's how life is supposed to be. You will make poor decisions in life — we all do — but it's what you do with the lessons learned that matters.
Think about every decision you've ever made. Were they always the best? Of course not. But look at how far you've come since then.

questions.prompt: What does the woman say about the food at the canteen?
options: It is absurdly expensive.
It is appropriately priced.
It brings shame on the university.
It caters to students and teachers.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the woman say about the food at the canteen? 

 【翻译】 女士对食堂的食物有何评价? 
 A)  价格高得离谱。 
 B)  定价合理。 
 C)  给大学丢脸。 
 D)  面向学生和教师提供服务。 

 【答案】 B （态度观点题） It is appropriately priced. 
 【定位】 P5 W: I don't, actually. I personally think they're perfectly appropriate. 
 女：其实我不同意。我个人觉得它们（价格）完全合理。 

 【信号】 被问者的直接应答 + 转折否定 。男士先抛出 the prices are absurd 并反问 Don't you agree，女士的应答 I don't, actually 是一句明确的否定回应，紧接 I personally think they're perfectly appropriate——『被问者的直接否定+亮明己见』正是答案句信号，女士的真实态度全在这句。 

 【替换】 perfectly appropriate ↔ appropriately priced 同根词改写：appropriate→appropriately priced 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 It is absurdly expensive. 直接挪用了录音里的 absurd，但说 the prices are absurd 的是男士、不是女士，女士恰恰否定了这一点。听到 absurd 就选 A，正中『听到原词就选』的陷阱。  借用原文：the prices are absurd 

 C) 原词陷阱 It brings shame on the university. 借用了录音里的 shame，但男士那句 Shame about the food. 是英式口语『可惜了这食物』的意思，并非『给学校丢脸』，且也不是女士对食物的评价。听到 shame 就联想到『丢脸』属于偷换概念。  借用原文：Shame about the food. 

 D) 答非所问 It caters to students and teachers. 挪用了录音 both for students and teachers，但那是男士在说食堂作为聚会点适合师生，谈的是场所、不是『食物』，与题目问的食物评价不沾边。  借用原文：both for students and teachers

questions.prompt: How does the woman feel about the canteen's sweet things or fancy delicacies?
options: They never really appeal to her.
They are never actually good value.
They are within students' budgets.
They always come at a high speed.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 How does the woman feel about the canteen's sweet things or fancy delicacies? 

 【翻译】 女士对食堂的甜食或精致美食有何感受? 
 A)  它们从来都不太吸引她。 
 B)  它们从来都不太物有所值。 
 C)  它们在学生的预算范围内。 
 D)  它们总是来得很快。 

 【答案】 A （态度观点题） They never really appeal to her. 
 【定位】 P7 I never really crave sweet things or any fancy delicacies. 
 我从来都不怎么想吃甜食或者什么精致美味。 

 【信号】 含蓄否定 never...crave 表态度 。女士说 I never really crave sweet things or any fancy delicacies，crave（渴望）配 never 是一句明确的『提不起兴趣』表态，正是答案信号——态度题就听这种带 never/really 的情感动词。 

 【替换】 I never really crave sweet things or any fancy delicacies ↔ They never really appeal to her. 主被动视角转换：我不想要它→它不吸引我 

 【排除】 B) 答非所问 They are never actually good value. 蹭了录音里关于价格的讨论（desserts are overpriced），但题目问的是女士对甜点的『感受/兴趣』，女士给出的态度是『不想吃』，而非评价它们『不划算』。把态度偷换成性价比。  借用原文：desserts are overpriced 

 C) 与原文相反 They are within students' budgets. 挪用了前文男士谈预算的 beyond most students' budgets，且与原文相反（男士说甜点超出预算），更何况它讲的是价格不是女士的态度，双重错位。  借用原文：beyond most students' budgets 

 D) 张冠李戴 They always come at a high speed. 借用了录音里关于上菜快的描述（They also come out really fast），但那是男士夸炒蛋出餐快，被安到了甜点和女士态度上，张冠李戴又答非所问。  借用原文：They also come out really fast

questions.prompt: What does the man say is one of the best things about the canteen?
options: The food.
The space.
The speed.
The environment.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the man say is one of the best things about the canteen? 

 【翻译】 男士说食堂最好的一点是什么? 
 A)  食物。 
 B)  空间。 
 C)  速度。 
 D)  环境。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） The speed. 
 【定位】 P8 Actually, that's one of the best things about the canteen — the speed. 
 其实，那是这个食堂最棒的一点之一——速度。 

 【信号】 最高级 one of the best 后直接点名 。男士说 that's one of the best things about the canteen — the speed，破折号后直接点出 the speed，是最高级语气+明确点名的答案信号，落点一目了然。 

 【替换】 the speed ↔ The speed. 原词直接对应 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 The food. 是全程反复出现的话题词，但男士对食物的评价是 the food is just OK，远谈不上『最好之一』，听到 food 高频出现就选属于被话题词诱导。  借用原文：the food is just OK 

 B) 答非所问 The space. 对应录音后文 It's a very versatile space，那是夸空间多用途，但并非男士点名的『best things』之一，落点不符。  借用原文：It's a very versatile space 

 D) 张冠李戴 The environment. 对应女士那句 it's such a great environment too，确实被夸，但夸环境的是女士、且不是男士点名的『最好之一』，张冠李戴又非答案落点。  借用原文：it's such a great environment too

questions.prompt: What did the canteen undergo a few years ago?
options: A complete refurnishing.
A ruinous burning down.
A substantial expansion.
A massive renovation.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What did the canteen undergo a few years ago? 

 【翻译】 食堂几年前经历了什么? 
 A)  全面重新装修。 
 B)  毁灭性的火灾。 
 C)  大规模扩建。 
 D)  大规模翻新。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） A massive renovation. 
 【定位】 P11 Apparently, they did a massive renovation a few years ago. 
 据说他们几年前做过一次大规模的翻新。 

 【信号】 时间状语 a few years ago 标记答案句 。女士说 they did a massive renovation a few years ago，时间状语 a few years ago 与题干完全对上，是答案句的定位信号；其谓语 did a massive renovation 即所问事件。 

 【替换】 a massive renovation ↔ A massive renovation. 原词对应，但需与近义项 expansion 切开 

 【排除】 A) 偷换概念 A complete refurnishing. 蹭了改造话题，但 refurnishing 是『重新配置家具』，与录音 a massive renovation（整体翻新）程度和性质都不同，是偷换概念。  借用原文：a massive renovation 

 B) 未提及 A ruinous burning down. 是『毁灭性烧毁』，录音通篇在夸食堂漂亮、做过翻新，根本没提任何火灾，纯属无中生有。 
 C) 偷换概念 A substantial expansion. 与答案 D 同样表『大规模』，借 massive/substantial 的近似制造混淆，但 expansion 是『扩建、变大』，录音说的是 renovation（翻新），并非扩大面积，差在动作名词上。  借用原文：a massive renovation

questions.prompt: According to the woman, what view about today's young people is not really justified?
options: They have a poor work ethic.
They don't get along with managers.
They are struggling in the workplace.
They aren't as varied as their predecessors.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 According to the woman, what view about today's young people is not really justified? 

 【翻译】 根据这位女士的说法,关于当今年轻人的哪种看法其实并不合理? 
 A)  他们的职业道德很差。 
 B)  他们与管理者相处不好。 
 C)  他们在职场中举步维艰。 
 D)  他们不如前辈那样多样化。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） They have a poor work ethic. 
 【定位】 P1 We often hear young people today have a poor work ethic. That's not really justified though, is it? 
 我们常听说如今的年轻人职业道德差。不过这种说法其实站不住脚，对吧？ 

 【信号】 女方自问句 + that's not justified 。答案句出自女方之口：先抛出常见说法 young people today have a poor work ethic，紧接 That's not really justified though 直接呼应题干的 not justified。「常听说……不过站不住脚」这个先立后破的句式，就是答案落点的信号。 

 【替换】 young people today have a poor work ethic ↔ They have a poor work ethic. 几乎原句搬到选项 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 选项 They don't get along with managers. 盗用了对话主题里反复出现的 managers，但女方在 P1 里判为「站不住脚」的说法是职业道德差，从没说年轻人和管理者合不来，属答非所问。  借用原文：young people today have a poor work ethic 

 C) 张冠李戴 选项 They are struggling in the workplace. 借了后文 if you are struggling to work with young people 里的 struggling，但那是说「管理者难以与年轻人共事」，并非女方在第 1 段判为不成立的看法，张冠李戴。  借用原文：if you are struggling to work with young people 

 D) 张冠李戴 选项 They aren't as varied as their predecessors. 与男方 young people of this age group are as varied and multifaceted as any other generation 正好相反：男方说「和任何一代一样多样」，选项却说「不如前人多样」，极性被反转，且这话也不是女方所说。  借用原文：as varied and multifaceted as any other generation

questions.prompt: What does the man say is important for managers to get along better with young workers?
options: Learning about the way they adhere to their own values.
Recognizing how they try to strike a work-life balance.
Knowing how they struggle to connect with managers.
Understanding the way they seek career advancement.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the man say is important for managers to get along better with young workers? 

 【翻译】 这位男士认为管理者要与年轻员工更好地相处,什么是重要的? 
 A)  了解他们坚持自己价值观的方式。 
 B)  认识到他们如何努力实现工作与生活的平衡。 
 C)  知道他们如何努力与管理者建立联系。 
 D)  理解他们寻求职业发展的方式。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Recognizing how they try to strike a work-life balance. 
 【定位】 P4 Well, it's essential to connect with them to learn about their values. It's also really important to recognize the way young people want to balance their work life with their personal life. 
 嗯，与他们建立联系、了解他们的价值观是必不可少的。同样很重要的是，认识到年轻人想要平衡工作与个人生活的方式。 

 【信号】 两个强调句 essential / important 。男方连用 it's essential to 和 It's also really important to recognize 两处强调，正面回答「什么重要」。题干落在 work-life balance 一支，对应的正是 recognize the way young people want to balance their work life with their personal life 这句。 

 【替换】 recognize the way young people want to balance their work life with their personal life ↔ Recognizing how they try to strike a work-life balance. balance their work...life=work-life balance 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 选项 Learning about the way they adhere to their own values. 盗用了 learn about their values 里的 values，可男方说的是「了解他们的价值观」，不是「了解他们如何坚守自己的价值观（adhere to）」，多塞了 adhere 这层原文没有的意思，答非所问。  借用原文：connect with them to learn about their values 

 C) 原词陷阱 选项 Knowing how they struggle to connect with managers. 把 connect with them 的 connect 与别处的 struggle、主题词 managers 拼到一起，但男方说的是「与他们建立联系去了解价值观」，从没说年轻人「难以与管理者建立联系」，纯属拼凑。  借用原文：it's essential to connect with them 

 D) 原词陷阱 选项 Understanding the way they seek career advancement. 借了 defer happiness in return for career advancement 的 career advancement，但那出自女方提问、且说的是年轻人「不愿」为升迁牺牲幸福；男方此处答「重要的是」并未把「理解他们如何追求升迁」列为关键，张冠李戴又答非所问。  借用原文：defer happiness in return for career advancement

questions.prompt: How do young people measure their productivity levels according to the man?
options: In terms of the number of hours spent.
By the amount of work they perform.
In terms of the work done in 8 hours.
By the quality of the work they do.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 How do young people measure their productivity levels according to the man? 

 【翻译】 根据这位男士的说法,年轻人如何衡量他们的生产力水平? 
 A)  根据花费的小时数。 
 B)  根据他们完成的工作量。 
 C)  根据8小时内完成的工作。 
 D)  根据他们所做工作的质量。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） By the quality of the work they do. 
 【定位】 P10 Generally, young people believe their productivity should not be measured by the number of hours they work, since someone can work for eight hours and accomplish next to nothing of significance for the company. Instead, young people measure their productivity levels by the quality of the work they perform. 
 一般来说，年轻人认为生产力不应以工作的小时数来衡量，因为有人可能干了八小时却几乎没为公司做出任何有意义的成果。相反，年轻人是以他们所做工作的质量来衡量生产力的。 

 【信号】 not…by hours, Instead…by quality 。男方先用 should not be measured by the number of hours 否定按时长，再用 Instead 引出真正口径 by the quality of the work they perform。Instead 之后才是答案落点，前半是被否定的干扰。 

 【替换】 by the quality of the work they perform ↔ By the quality of the work they do. perform=do，其余原样 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 选项 In terms of the number of hours spent. 几乎照搬 the number of hours they work，但这恰恰是男方用 should not be measured 明确否定掉的口径，选它正中陷阱。  借用原文：should not be measured by the number of hours they work 

 B) 偷换概念 选项 By the amount of work they perform. 借了原文的 work、perform，但把口径换成「工作的数量（amount）」，男方说的是质量而非数量，偷换了概念。  借用原文：the quality of the work they perform 

 C) 原词陷阱 选项 In terms of the work done in 8 hours. 盗用 work for eight hours 的 eight hours，但那只是男方举例说明「干八小时也可能毫无成果」、用来反证不该按时长，并非衡量口径本身，答非所问。  借用原文：someone can work for eight hours and accomplish next to nothing

questions.prompt: What companies does the man think would appeal to young workers?
options: Those whose culture facilitates their advancement.
Those allowing them to do projects of their choice.
Those whose values align with their own.
Those refraining from discrediting their perspectives.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What companies does the man think would appeal to young workers? 

 【翻译】 这位男士认为什么样的公司会吸引年轻员工? 
 A)  那些其文化有助于他们晋升的公司。 
 B)  那些允许他们做自己选择的项目的公司。 
 C)  那些其价值观与他们自己的价值观一致的公司。 
 D)  那些避免贬低他们观点的公司。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） Those whose values align with their own. 
 【定位】 P12 Young workers want to work on projects that matter to themselves, the company or the world at large. They must feel the need to stay working at a company whose values align with their own. 
 年轻员工想做对自己、对公司或对整个世界都有意义的项目。他们必然会想留在一家价值观与自己一致的公司。 

 【信号】 末段总结句 a company whose values align 。对话收尾男方给出结论 stay working at a company whose values align with their own，直接定义了吸引年轻人的公司类型。这是对话末尾的总结落点，正面回答题干。 

 【替换】 a company whose values align with their own ↔ Those whose values align with their own. a company=Those，定语原样 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 选项 Those whose culture facilitates their advancement. 把主题氛围词 culture 与女方提问里的 career advancement 拼合，但男方末段说的是「价值观一致」，从没说公司文化要「助推升迁」，纯属拼凑且不是结论。  借用原文：defer happiness in return for career advancement 

 B) 偷换概念 选项 Those allowing them to do projects of their choice. 盗用 work on projects that matter 的 projects，可男方说的是做「有意义的（matter）」项目，不是「他们自选的（of their choice）」项目，偷偷改了限定，与原文不符。  借用原文：work on projects that matter to themselves, the company or the world at large 

 D) 原词陷阱 选项 Those refraining from discrediting their perspectives. 借了 Such a perspective can be hard to discredit 的 discredit、perspective，但那是女方提问里说「这种看法很难被否定」，并非男方对「吸引人的公司」给出的特征，张冠李戴。  借用原文：Such a perspective can be hard to discredit, can't it?

questions.prompt: What does a new study suggest about restaurants including vegetarian sections on their menus?
options: They may unconsciously help customers choose greener dishes.
They may unintentionally encourage customers to eat meat.
They raise customers' environmental awareness.
They enable customers to eat in a healthy way.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does a new study suggest about restaurants including vegetarian sections on their menus? 

 【翻译】 一项新研究对餐厅在菜单上包含素食区域有何看法? 
 A)  它们可能会无意识地帮助顾客选择更环保的菜品。 
 B)  它们可能会无意中鼓励顾客吃肉。 
 C)  它们提高了顾客的环保意识。 
 D)  它们使顾客能够以健康的方式进食。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） They may unintentionally encourage customers to eat meat. 
 【定位】 P1 Although it sounds counter-intuitive, restaurants which include specific vegetarian sections on their menus may be unintentionally encouraging customers to eat meat, a new study suggests. 
 尽管听起来有违直觉，但一项新研究表明，在菜单上专门设素食专区的餐厅，可能正无意中鼓励顾客去吃肉。 

 【信号】 让步转折Although后是真意 。句首 Although it sounds counter-intuitive（尽管听起来违反直觉）是让步信号，真正的研究结论在它之后——may be unintentionally encouraging customers to eat meat，加上 a new study suggests 与题干 suggest 对应，这就是答案句。 

 【替换】 unintentionally encouraging customers to eat meat ↔ unintentionally encourage customers to eat meat 近乎同形的直接对应 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 A说"无意中帮顾客选更环保的菜"，盗用了开头 moving away from environmentally unfriendly meat towards greener dishes 里的 greener，但那是"餐厅想达到的初衷"，研究的发现恰恰相反——是鼓励吃肉，A把结果方向说反了。  借用原文：moving away from environmentally unfriendly meat towards greener dishes 

 C) 未提及 C说"提高顾客的环保意识"，听上去与开头 eat more sustainably 沾边，但录音从没说研究发现能"提升意识"，只谈"实际点菜选择"，属于顺着环保话题硬编出来的结论。 
 D) 未提及 D说"让顾客以健康方式进食"，但全篇围绕"环保/吃肉还是吃素"，从未谈"健康"这个角度，属于另起话题的无中生有。

questions.prompt: How was the study carried out on 750 participants?
options: By inviting them to taste different kinds of food.
By observing the eating behavior of strict vegetarians.
By comparing participants eating vegetarian food frequently with those doing so rarely.
By requiring participants to choose a meal as if they were feasting at a family gathering.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 How was the study carried out on 750 participants? 

 【翻译】 对750名参与者进行的研究是如何开展的? 
 A)  通过邀请他们品尝不同种类的食物。 
 B)  通过观察严格素食者的饮食行为。 
 C)  通过比较经常食用素食的参与者与很少这样做的参与者。 
 D)  通过要求参与者选择一餐,就好像他们正在家庭聚会上用餐一样。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） By comparing participants eating vegetarian food frequently with those doing so rarely. 
 【定位】 P2 The study involved 750 people, half of whom frequently ate vegetarian food and half of whom rarely ate it. No vegetarians were included. 
 研究共有750人参与，其中一半人经常吃素食，另一半人很少吃素食。没有素食者被纳入研究。 

 【信号】 数字750与分组描述句 。听到题干里的数字 750 出现在 The study involved 750 people，紧跟其后的 half of whom frequently ate vegetarian food and half of whom rarely ate it 正是研究设计的核心——把人分成"常吃素"和"很少吃素"两组对比，这就是答案句。 

 【替换】 half of whom frequently ate vegetarian food and half of whom rarely ate it ↔ comparing participants eating vegetarian food frequently with those doing so rarely 对照设计的同义改写 

 【排除】 A) 偷换概念 A说"请他们品尝不同食物"，但录音只让受试者"看菜单选一餐"given different menus and asked to choose a meal，并没有真去吃/尝，属把"选菜单"偷换成"尝食物"。  借用原文：given different menus and asked to choose a meal 

 B) 与原文相反 B说"观察严格素食者的进食行为"，盗用了原文反复出现的 vegetarian，但录音明说 No vegetarians were included——根本没有素食者参加，更没有"观察其行为"，与原文相反。  借用原文：No vegetarians were included 

 D) 原词陷阱 D说"要求受试者像在家庭聚会上盛宴那样选餐"，盗用了 asked to choose a meal，但原文的设定是 as if they were eating out with friends（像和朋友外出就餐），不是"家庭聚会盛宴"，场景被偷换。  借用原文：asked to choose a meal as if they were eating out with friends

questions.prompt: How do altered menu designs affect frequent eaters of vegetarian food?
options: They are less likely to choose a vegetarian dish.
They find vegetarian dishes become more appealing.
They tend to consume larger portions of unhealthy food.
They are less likely to choose dishes recommended by chefs.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 How do altered menu designs affect frequent eaters of vegetarian food? 

 【翻译】 改变后的菜单设计如何影响经常食用素食的人? 
 A)  他们不太可能选择素食菜品。 
 B)  他们发现素食菜品变得更有吸引力。 
 C)  他们倾向于食用更大份量的不健康食物。 
 D)  他们不太可能选择厨师推荐的菜品。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） They are less likely to choose a vegetarian dish. 
 【定位】 P2 But again, these altered menu designs backfired with those who ate vegetarian food more frequently, leading them to be less likely to choose a vegetarian dish. 
 但同样地，这些改动过的菜单设计对那些更常吃素食的人产生了反效果，使他们更不可能去选一道素菜。 

 【信号】 But again转折指向常吃者 。But again 是转折信号，前一句讲改菜单让"少吃素的人"更愿点素菜，转折之后才轮到题目问的"常吃素的人"——backfired with those who ate vegetarian food more frequently，结果是 less likely to choose a vegetarian dish，这就是答案句。 

 【替换】 less likely to choose a vegetarian dish ↔ less likely to choose a vegetarian dish 几乎逐字一致 

 【排除】 B) 张冠李戴 B说"他们觉得素菜更有吸引力"，盗用了原文 a more appealing description of a non-meat meal 里的 appealing，但"更想点素菜"这个正向结果发生在"少吃素的人"身上，题目问的"常吃素的人"恰恰相反，张冠李戴。  借用原文：a more appealing description of a non-meat meal 

 C) 未提及 C说"他们会吃更多不健康食物"，但录音只谈"是否点素菜"，从没提"吃更大份的不健康食物"，属凭印象编出来的结果。 
 D) 原词陷阱 D说"他们更不可能点主厨推荐的菜"，盗用了原文 presenting a vegetarian dish as the chef's recommendation 里的 chef，但原文说的结果是"更不可能点素菜"，而非"不点主厨推荐的菜"，把对象从"素菜"偷换成"主厨推荐菜"。  借用原文：presenting a vegetarian dish as the chef's recommendation

questions.prompt: What does the passage say about Nottingham Trent University and the Chinese Academy of Sciences?
options: They have found a solution to the global problem of air pollution.
They have managed to freeze polluting particles to around –18 °C.
They have been seeking a way to prevent pollutants from penetrating indoors.
They have been cooperating closely on developing a new type of air-conditioner.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the passage say about Nottingham Trent University and the Chinese Academy of Sciences? 

 【翻译】 文章关于诺丁汉特伦特大学和中国科学院说了什么? 
 A)  它们找到了解决全球空气污染问题的方案。 
 B)  它们成功地将污染颗粒冷冻到零下18摄氏度左右。 
 C)  它们一直在寻求防止污染物渗入室内的方法。 
 D)  它们一直在密切合作研发一种新型空调。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） They have been seeking a way to prevent pollutants from penetrating indoors. 
 【定位】 P1 Nottingham Trent University and the Chinese Academy of Sciences have been trying to find a way to prevent deadly outdoor air pollution from penetrating indoors. 
 诺丁汉特伦特大学与中国科学院一直在设法找到一种途径，阻止致命的室外空气污染渗入室内。 

 【信号】 段首总述句 。录音开篇第一句就以两家机构为主语作总述：have been trying to find a way to prevent deadly outdoor air pollution from penetrating indoors，篇章独白的研究目的常在段首点明，这句正是答案句。 

 【替换】 have been trying to find a way ↔ have been seeking a way trying to find = seeking 
 prevent deadly outdoor air pollution from penetrating indoors ↔ prevent pollutants from penetrating indoors 几乎原句保留 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 A 项盗用了第二段的 global problem 一词，说他们已 found a solution to the global problem，但录音用的是 trying to find a way（还在尝试），并未说已彻底解决全球性难题，把探索说成了已完成，程度过满。  借用原文：Outdoor air pollution in cities is a global problem 

 B) 原词陷阱 B 项盗用录音第二句的原词 frozen to around –18，但 –18 ℃ 冷冻只是实现目标的手段细节，题目问的是这两家机构在做什么（目的），用手段冒充目的，答非所问。  借用原文：if pollution is frozen to around –18 ℃ in a condensing tube 

 D) 偷换概念 D 项说两家在合作开发一种新型空调（developing a new type of air-conditioner）；录音只说有望对现有空调做 simple modification of air conditioning units（简单改造），从未说开发新空调，是无中生有式偷换。  借用原文：simple modification of air conditioning units so that they can also clean polluted indoor air

questions.prompt: What do we learn from the passage about existing technologies to purify indoor air?
options: They can be costly and inefficient.
They are constantly being perfected.
They are by-products of health research.
They can save over 40,000 lives each year.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn from the passage about existing technologies to purify indoor air? 

 【翻译】 从文章中我们了解到关于现有净化室内空气技术的什么信息? 
 A)  它们可能成本高昂且效率低下。 
 B)  它们正在不断完善。 
 C)  它们是健康研究的副产品。 
 D)  它们每年可以挽救超过四万人的生命。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） They can be costly and inefficient. 
 【定位】 P2 While there are some existing technologies to purify indoor air, they can be inefficient, expensive or produce harmful by-products. 
 虽然已有一些净化室内空气的现有技术，但它们可能低效、昂贵，或产生有害的副产品。 

 【信号】 While 让步后转折出真意 。句子以 While there are some existing technologies 让步开头，承认有现有技术，紧接着的 they can be inefficient, expensive 才是真正要说的评价；让步与转折之后的部分是答案落点。 

 【替换】 expensive ↔ costly expensive = costly 
 inefficient ↔ inefficient 低效原词对应 

 【排除】 B) 与原文相反 B 项说现有技术 constantly being perfected（不断完善），是正面评价；但录音对它的评价是 inefficient, expensive or produce harmful by-products（负面），极性正好弄反。  借用原文：they can be inefficient, expensive or produce harmful by-products 

 C) 偷换概念 C 项盗用录音原词 by-products，但录音说的是现有技术可能 produce harmful by-products（产生有害副产品），C 却说它们本身是健康研究的副产品（by-products of health research），张冠李戴改了主体关系。  借用原文：produce harmful by-products 

 D) 原词陷阱 D 项盗用录音的醒目数字 40,000，说现有技术每年能救四万多人；但录音里 40,000 讲的是 over 40,000 early deaths in Britain each year（每年四万多人过早死亡），是死亡数而非现有技术挽救的人数，数字对象被错配。  借用原文：pollution is linked to over 40,000 early deaths in Britain each year

questions.prompt: What do people tend to do when outdoor air quality is poor?
options: They keep their windows closed.
They spend a lot more time indoors.
They make more use of air-conditioners.
They try various ways to purify indoor air.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do people tend to do when outdoor air quality is poor? 

 【翻译】 当室外空气质量差时,人们往往会做什么? 
 A)  他们关闭窗户。 
 B)  他们在室内待的时间更长。 
 C)  他们更多地使用空调。 
 D)  他们尝试各种方法净化室内空气。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） They spend a lot more time indoors. 
 【定位】 P2 When outdoor air quality is poor, people tend to spend even more time indoors. 
 当户外空气质量差时，人们往往会在室内待更长时间。 

 【信号】 题干原词 tend to 直接对应 。录音里 When outdoor air quality is poor, people tend to spend even more time indoors 与题干用词几乎一字不差，tend to 这一标志词直接锁定答案句，属顺序定位。 

 【替换】 spend even more time indoors ↔ spend a lot more time indoors even more = a lot more 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 A 项说人们关窗（keep their windows closed），听起来很合常识，但录音从头到尾没提到关窗这个动作，属凭常识脑补、原文未提及。 
 C) 未提及 C 项说人们更多用空调（make more use of air-conditioners），录音里 air conditioning 是讲技术改造方向，并未说人们在空气差时更多使用空调，属常识脑补、原文未提及人们这一行为。 
 D) 张冠李戴 D 项盗用话题原词 purify indoor air，但录音里净化室内空气是技术/研究要做的事，不是人们在空气差时采取的做法，主体被张冠李戴。  借用原文：While there are some existing technologies to purify indoor air

questions.prompt: What did Professor Gang Pan of the Chinese Academy of Sciences say about their study?
options: It shows the importance of eliminating indoor pollution.
It may change the way of future environmental research.
It demonstrates the fruitful cooperation between UK and Chinese scientists.
It may make household appliances serve an additional air cleaner function.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What did Professor Gang Pan of the Chinese Academy of Sciences say about their study? 

 【翻译】 中国科学院的潘刚教授关于他们的研究说了什么? 
 A)  它显示了消除室内污染的重要性。 
 B)  它可能改变未来环境研究的方式。 
 C)  它展示了中英科学家之间富有成效的合作。 
 D)  它可能使家用电器发挥额外的空气净化功能。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） It may make household appliances serve an additional air cleaner function. 
 【定位】 P2 Our study makes it possible to add an air cleaner option to household appliances in areas which might experience extremely poor air conditions. 
 我们的研究使得在空气质量可能极差的地区，给家用电器增加一项空气净化功能成为可能。 

 【信号】 专家引语中的用途句 。在专家 Professor Gang Pan 的引语里，Our study makes it possible to add an air cleaner option to household appliances 直接点出研究的实际用途，是被引用原话中评价研究意义的关键句，即答案句。 

 【替换】 add an air cleaner option to household appliances ↔ make household appliances serve an additional air cleaner function add option = additional function 

 【排除】 A) 过度推断 A 项说研究显示了消除室内污染的重要性（importance of eliminating indoor pollution）；录音里专家说的是 By controlling indoor air pollution（控制污染）并讲其用途，并未把重点放在论证消除污染有多重要上，A 拔高且偏离原话。  借用原文：By controlling indoor air pollution and improving air quality in this way 

 B) 过度推断 B 项说研究可能改变未来环境研究的方式（change the way of future environmental research），录音里专家只谈本研究的用途与对公共健康的好处，从未说会改变未来研究的方式，属无中生有的拔高。 
 C) 原词陷阱 C 项说研究证明了中英科学家的成功合作（cooperation between UK and Chinese scientists），录音开头确有两家机构合作的事实 Nottingham Trent University and the Chinese Academy of Sciences，但题目问专家对研究本身说了什么，专家原话谈的是用途而非合作，借合作事实答非所问。  借用原文：Nottingham Trent University and the Chinese Academy of Sciences have been trying to find a way

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the well-known mirror test?
options: It distinguishes different species of animals.
It reflects distinct traits in animal behavior.
It demonstrates animals' ability to recognize themselves.
It gauges the level of intelligence of various animal species.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn about the well-known mirror test? 

 【翻译】 关于著名的镜像测试，我们了解到什么？ 
 A)  它可以区分不同的动物物种。 
 B)  它反映了动物行为的不同特征。 
 C)  它展示了动物识别自身的能力。 
 D)  它衡量各种动物物种的智力水平。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） It demonstrates animals' ability to recognize themselves. 
 【定位】 P2 This is a test that demonstrates self-recognition in animals. Only a few animals, such as humans, apes, dolphins and some birds, can recognize themselves in a mirror. 
 这是一项检验动物自我识别能力的测试。只有少数动物，例如人类、猿、海豚和某些鸟类，能在镜子里认出自己。 

 【信号】 下定义句 This is a test that… 。录音用 This is a test that demonstrates self-recognition in animals 这样的"This is a test that…"下定义句式，直接点出测试的功能，这种"给某物下定义"的句子就是细节题的答案句信号。 

 【替换】 demonstrates self-recognition in animals ↔ demonstrates animals' ability to recognize themselves 名词↔动词的同义改写 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 录音里确实念到 A certain species of fish 的 species（物种），选项 distinguishes different species of animals 就盗用这个词造"分辨物种"，但测试是测"自我识别"，不是分辨物种，听到 species 就选会中招。  借用原文：A certain species of fish 

 B) 偷换概念 录音通篇讲 behavior、behavioral，选项 reflects distinct traits in animal behavior 盗用 behavior 造"反映行为的不同特征"，但测试反映的是"能否自我识别"，不是"区分行为差异"，概念被悄悄换掉。  借用原文：This ability suggests a level of higher intelligence and awareness 

 D) 过度推断 录音说 This ability suggests a level of higher intelligence，选项 gauges the level of intelligence of various animal species 盗用 intelligence 和 level 造"测量各物种智力等级"，但原文是"自我识别这种能力暗示了较高智力"，测试本身测的是自我识别，不是给智力分级。  借用原文：This ability suggests a level of higher intelligence and awareness

questions.prompt: What does the study by the speaker's team show about the fish they experimented with?
options: It meets few of the behavioral criteria set in the mirror test.
It behaves similarly to animals capable of self-recognition.
It removes marks from itself to show self-awareness.
It matches children over 18 months in intelligence.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the study by the speaker's team show about the fish they experimented with? 

 【翻译】 演讲者团队对所实验鱼类的研究表明了什么？ 
 A)  它仅符合镜像测试中设定的少数几项行为标准。 
 B)  它的行为与能够自我识别的动物相似。 
 C)  它通过清除自身的标记来表现自我意识。 
 D)  它的智力相当于超过18个月的儿童。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） It behaves similarly to animals capable of self-recognition. 
 【定位】 P2 The behaviors we observe leave little doubt that this fish behaviorally fulfills all criteria of the mirror test as originally laid out. 
 我们观察到的行为几乎可以确定，这条鱼在行为上满足了最初设定的镜子测试的全部标准。 

 【信号】 结果断言 leave little doubt that… 。录音用 leave little doubt that this fish behaviorally fulfills all criteria"几乎无疑地满足全部标准"这种强结果断言，是实验给出的核心结论，正是答案句信号。 

 【替换】 fulfills all criteria of the mirror test ↔ behaves similarly to animals capable of self-recognition 满足标准=行为同已通过者 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 录音念到 criteria，但说的是 fulfills all criteria（满足全部标准），选项 meets few of the behavioral criteria 盗用 criteria 却改成"几乎不满足"，把肯定听成了否定，正好反了。  借用原文：fulfills all criteria of the mirror test 

 C) 偷换概念 录音确有 scrape up against hard surfaces to remove marks"蹭掉身上标记"，选项 removes marks from itself to show self-awareness 盗用 remove marks，但把它直接等同于"展示自我意识"——而录音第三段明说"是否算自我意识尚不清楚"，这是把现象当定论，偷换了概念。  借用原文：scrape up against hard surfaces to remove marks placed on its body 

 D) 张冠李戴 录音 This is not shown by children until around 18 months 里的 18 个月是说"人类儿童到约18个月才有此能力"，选项 matches children over 18 months in intelligence 盗用这个数字，硬说"鱼的智力等同18个月以上的儿童"，把讲儿童的话安到鱼头上。  借用原文：This is not shown by children until around 18 months

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about the results of their research?
options: They have conclusively established the criteria of animal intelligence.
They have advanced the concept of self-awareness to a higher level.
They incorporate more perspectives than one.
They raise more questions than answers.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker say about the results of their research? 

 【翻译】 关于他们的研究结果，演讲者说了什么？ 
 A)  他们已经确凿地确立了评判动物智力的标准。 
 B)  他们将自我意识这一概念提升到了更高的层次。 
 C)  他们包含了不止一种观点。 
 D)  它们引发的问题多于给出的答案。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） They raise more questions than answers. 
 【定位】 P4 Results from our research raise more questions than answers. 
 我们研究得出的结果，带来的问题比答案还多。 

 【信号】 结尾定调句 Results… raise… 。末段以 Results from our research raise more questions than answers 开篇，是讲者对整项研究结果的收束定调，这种"结尾一句话总评结果"正是答案句信号。 

 【替换】 raise more questions than answers ↔ They raise more questions than answers. 近乎原句对应 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 录音多次提 criteria，选项 conclusively established the criteria of animal intelligence 盗用并说"已确凿确立动物智力标准"，但末段恰恰说"问题更多"、还呼吁 stop looking at responses to the mirror as a decisive test，根本没"确立"，反了。  借用原文：stop looking at responses to the mirror as a decisive test 

 B) 过度推断 录音满是 self-awareness，选项 advanced the concept of self-awareness to a higher level 盗用这个词造"把自我意识概念提升到更高层次"，听着很顺，但录音说的是结果带来更多疑问、要换更丰富的理论，并未声称"提升了概念层次"。  借用原文：Only with a richer theory of the self and a larger test battery will we be able to determine all of the various levels of self-awareness 

 C) 未提及 选项 incorporate more perspectives than one 和正确项 raise more questions than answers 都是 more…than… 句式，长得像；但录音结果说的是"问题比答案多"，没说"纳入多个视角"，C 是借相似句式硬凑、原文无对应。

questions.prompt: What finding from the new study might come as a huge surprise?
options: Small children are even more keen on screens than their elders.
Both parents and children preferred to read electronic books.
Parents differed from children in reading behavior.
Children reading electronic books learned more.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What finding from the new study might come as a huge surprise? 

 【翻译】 这项新研究的哪一发现可能会令人极为意外？ 
 A)  小孩子甚至比他们的长辈更热衷于屏幕。 
 B)  父母和孩子都更喜欢阅读电子书。 
 C)  父母的阅读行为与孩子不同。 
 D)  阅读电子书的孩子学到的东西更多。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Children reading electronic books learned more. 
 【定位】 P1 So the finding from a new study that very young children enjoy electronic books more than printed picture books may not come as a huge surprise — but the following additional findings might: both parents and children behaved differently when reading electronic versus printed picture books. And the children who read the electronic books learned more. 
 因此，一项新研究发现幼儿比起纸质图画书更喜欢电子书，这一点也许并不令人意外——但接下来这些额外发现就可能令人意外了：父母和孩子在读电子书与纸质书时表现各不相同；而且读电子书的孩子学到的更多。 

 【信号】 转折 but…might 指向真正的意外 。录音先用 may not come as a huge surprise 把"小孩爱电子书"排掉，紧接 but the following additional findings might 一个转折，明确告诉你"意外的发现"在 but 之后；冒号后并列两条，其中 the children who read the electronic books learned more 正是答案落点。 

 【替换】 the children who read the electronic books learned more ↔ Children reading electronic books learned more 近乎同义、仅句式微调 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 Small children are even more keen on screens than their elders. 借用了录音 small children are generally keen on screens 的原词，但录音说这是"也许并不令人意外"的前提，与题面要的"意外发现"正相反，听到 keen on screens 就选会中招。  借用原文：small children are generally keen on screens 

 B) 偷换概念 Both parents and children preferred to read electronic books. 套用了录音 both parents and children behaved differently 里的 both parents and children，却把 behaved differently（表现不同）偷换成 preferred to read electronic books（都偏爱电子书），原文从没说父母也偏爱电子书。  借用原文：both parents and children behaved differently 

 C) 答非所问 Parents differed from children in reading behavior. 确实对应 both parents and children behaved differently，本身没说错，但题干特别问"令人意外"的发现，录音的 surprise 落点落在"孩子学得更多"上；C 是 but 后并列的发现之一，却不是题面聚焦的那一条，被更贴题的 D 比下去。  借用原文：both parents and children behaved differently

questions.prompt: What do we learn about previous studies of young children reading electronic books?
options: They came to conflicting conclusions.
They were based on small samples.
They yielded unanticipated findings.
They were focused on younger kids.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn about previous studies of young children reading electronic books? 

 【翻译】 关于幼儿阅读电子书的以往研究，我们了解到什么？ 
 A)  它们得出了相互矛盾的结论。 
 B)  它们以小规模样本为基础。 
 C)  它们得出了出乎意料的结果。 
 D)  它们关注的是年龄更小的孩子。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） They came to conflicting conclusions. 
 【定位】 P2 In fact, multiple studies have found that electronic books support story comprehension and vocabulary gains beyond what is provided by printed books. But there's also work suggesting that children sometimes invest less mental effort in learning from electronic books, and that parents talk less about content when sharing such books. 
 事实上，多项研究发现，电子书在故事理解和词汇增长上的助益超过纸质书。但也有研究表明，孩子有时在电子书上投入的脑力反而更少，父母在一起读这类书时谈论内容也更少。 

 【信号】 but 把两拨研究结论正反对置 。录音先说 multiple studies have found that electronic books support story comprehension and vocabulary gains（电子书有利），再用 But there's also work suggesting that children sometimes invest less mental effort（也有研究说不利）一转，正反两拨研究结论摆在一起——这正是"结论相互矛盾"的信号。 

 【替换】 multiple studies have found that electronic books support story comprehension and vocabulary gains ↔ They came to conflicting conclusions 正反两面概括为"矛盾" 

 【排除】 B) 未提及 They were based on small samples. 谈以往研究的样本量，但录音讲 previous studies 时只对比了结论方向，全程没说过样本大小，属凭"评价研究常谈样本"的常识硬填。 
 C) 张冠李戴 They yielded unanticipated findings. 里 unanticipated 蹭了第 1 段 huge surprise 的"意外"概念，但那是形容"本次新研究"的发现；本题问的是 previous studies（以往研究），张冠李戴。  借用原文：but the following additional findings might 

 D) 偷换概念 They were focused on younger kids. 借了录音反复出现的 young children 概念，但录音说的是"也有针对 older children 的研究"，并未限定以往研究都只盯更小的孩子，把研究对象范围说窄了。  借用原文：there's research on older children

questions.prompt: What extra features should be included in electronic books to bolster children's learning?
options: Those that prove simple enough for them to comprehend.
Those that produce both audio and visual effects on them.
Those that draw their attention to the educational content.
Those that contribute to their increased interest in reading.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What extra features should be included in electronic books to bolster children's learning? 

 【翻译】 电子书中应加入哪些额外功能来促进儿童学习？ 
 A)  那些足够简单、便于他们理解的功能。 
 B)  那些能同时对他们产生听觉和视觉效果的功能。 
 C)  那些能将他们的注意力吸引到教育内容上的功能。 
 D)  那些有助于提高他们阅读兴趣的功能。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） Those that draw their attention to the educational content. 
 【定位】 P6 Extra features in electronic books may increase children's participation with them; however, if these features don't draw attention to the educational content, they may not serve as a supportive feature. 
 电子书里的额外功能也许能提高孩子的参与度；然而，如果这些功能不能把注意力引向教育内容，它们就可能起不到辅助作用。 

 【信号】 however + if 否定句给出条件 。录音先承认 Extra features…may increase children's participation，再用 however, if these features don't draw attention to the educational content, they may not serve as a supportive feature 反转——用"如果不指向教育内容就没用"反推出"要指向教育内容才有用"，答案落在 if 否定句里。 

 【替换】 if these features don't draw attention to the educational content, they may not serve as a supportive feature ↔ Those that draw their attention to the educational content 否定条件转正面、原词点对 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 Those that prove simple enough for them to comprehend. 蹭了第 5 段 the electronic books in the study were simple 的 simple，但那只是描述研究所用电子书的特点，录音从没说"简单到能懂"是促进学习该加的功能，听到 simple 就选会落坑。  借用原文：the electronic books in the study were simple 

 B) 原词陷阱 Those that produce both audio and visual effects on them. 直接搬录音 they included background music, animation and sound effects 的音乐、动画、音效，这些恰是"声光效果"，但录音的落点是"光有这些额外功能、若不指向教育内容就没用"，B 把被否定的诱饵当成了答案。  借用原文：they included background music, animation and sound effects 

 D) 偷换概念 Those that contribute to their increased interest in reading. 像是改写自录音 Extra features…may increase children's participation，但录音说的是 increase participation（提高参与度），并把它和"促进学习"区分开（参与高未必学得好），选项把它换成 increased interest in reading（提高阅读兴趣）且当成促学习的条件，偷换且跑题。  借用原文：Extra features in electronic books may increase children's participation with them

questions.prompt: What should we do with the unfavorable decisions we've made?
options: Regret having wasted much time in making them.
Think how different we could have made them.
Keep ourselves from regretting them.
Live with them for the time being.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What should we do with the unfavorable decisions we've made? 

 【翻译】 我们应该如何看待自己所作出的那些不理想的决定？ 
 A)  后悔在作出这些决定时浪费了很多时间。 
 B)  想想我们本可以把这些决定变得多么不同。 
 C)  不要让自己后悔这些决定。 
 D)  暂时接受这些决定。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） Keep ourselves from regretting them. 
 【定位】 P1 If you're living your life full of regrets, you're wasting your time. ... There are plenty of unfavorable decisions we've made, but does that mean we should regret them? No! 
 如果你的人生充满后悔，那就是在浪费时间。……我们确实做过很多不理想的决定，但这是否意味着我们该为之后悔呢？不！ 

 【信号】 反问加 No 的强烈否定 。does that mean we should regret them? No! 用'反问 + 斩钉截铁的 No'把态度顶到最高：不该后悔。这种自问自答后紧跟否定的句子，正是演讲者亮出主张的答案信号。 

 【替换】 does that mean we should regret them? No! ↔ Keep ourselves from regretting them '不该后悔'＝'避免后悔' 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 A 把原文里 living your life full of regrets, you're wasting your time 的两个原词 regret 和 wasting time 拼到一起，做成 Regret having wasted much time in making them.，但原文说'后悔本身是浪费时间'，A 却变成'为浪费时间而后悔'，听到原词就选必中招。  借用原文：living your life full of regrets, you're wasting your time 

 B) 与原文相反 原文 just because things could be different, it doesn't necessarily mean they would be better 是在否定'设想不同会更好'，B 项 Think how different we could have made them. 却把这件被否定的事当成'应该做的'，正话反说，与原意相左。  借用原文：just because things could be different, it doesn't necessarily mean they would be better 

 D) 未提及 Live with them for the time being. 主张'暂且与这些决定共处'，但原文从头到尾讲的是'别后悔、向前看'，并没有说'暂且忍受'这种过渡性态度，属于无中生有。

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about every single decision we've ever made?
options: It has made us the person we are now.
It has been made with a lot of thinking.
It stems from our valuable knowledge.
It benefits us greatly one way or another.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker say about every single decision we've ever made? 

 【翻译】 关于我们曾经作出的每一个决定，讲话者说了什么？ 
 A)  它造就了如今的我们。 
 B)  它是在经过深思熟虑后作出的。 
 C)  它源于我们宝贵的知识。 
 D)  无论以何种方式，它都对我们大有裨益。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） It has made us the person we are now. 
 【定位】 P3 Every single decision you've ever made, positive or negative, has made you the person you are today. 
 你做过的每一个决定，无论好坏，都造就了今天的你。 

 【信号】 题干原词在句首直接成句 。原文 Every single decision you've ever made, positive or negative, has made you the person you are today 句首即题干原话 every single decision，紧接着的 has made you the person you are today 就是对它的评价，是直接成句的答案信号。 

 【替换】 has made you the person you are today ↔ It has made us the person we are now 几乎同义、仅人称与 today/now 替换 

 【排除】 B) 未提及 It has been made with a lot of thinking. 说决定是'经过大量思考做出的'，但原文评价决定时说的是它'造就了今天的你'，并没有谈决定是否深思熟虑，属无中生有。 
 C) 原词陷阱 C 搬来原文 the valuable knowledge from the lessons we learned 里的 valuable knowledge，做成 It stems from our valuable knowledge.，但原文是说'回到过去会失去这份宝贵知识'，并非说决定'源自'知识，盗原词且因果方向反了。  借用原文：the valuable knowledge from the lessons we learned 

 D) 答非所问 It benefits us greatly one way or another. 说决定'总能大大有益'，虽与全篇基调沾边，但原文评价 every single decision 的具体说法是'造就了今天的你'，D 是脱离答案句的笼统概括，并非演讲者此处的原话。  借用原文：Every single decision you've ever made, positive or negative, has made you the person you are today

questions.prompt: What is life full of according to the speaker?
options: Challenging things to do.
Beautiful things to share.
Choices to make.
Lessons to learn.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is life full of according to the speaker? 

 【翻译】 讲话者认为生活充满了什么？ 
 A)  需要去做的具有挑战性的事情。 
 B)  值得分享的美好事物。 
 C)  需要作出的选择。 
 D)  需要吸取的教训。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Lessons to learn. 
 【定位】 P5 Life is full of lessons to learn, so we can't let regret stop us from moving forward. 
 人生充满了需要汲取的教训，所以我们不能让后悔阻挡自己前进。 

 【信号】 题干句式原样出现 。原文 Life is full of lessons to learn 与题干句式 full of 一字不差，紧跟其后的 lessons to learn 即是要填的中心词，是句式复刻型的答案信号。 

 【替换】 Life is full of lessons to learn ↔ Lessons to learn 原句中心词直接对应选项 

 【排除】 C) 原词陷阱 Choices to make. 借了原文反复出现的 the choices you do 里的 choices，与 decisions 近义、特别像，但 full of 后面原文念的是 lessons to learn 不是 choices，听到近义词就选会被换走。  借用原文：the choices you do 

 A) 未提及 Challenging things to do. 形式上凑成并列项，但原文 full of 后并没有念 challenging things，演讲者也没说人生充满挑战，属于未提及。 
 B) 未提及 Beautiful things to share. 听起来很正能量，但原文 full of 后是 lessons to learn，从未提'美好的可分享之物'，靠基调相近蒙人。

questions.prompt: What is said to be of real importance when we make poor decisions in life?
options: Foreseeing the possibility for regret later.
Making proper use of the lessons learned.
Perfecting the decision-making strategies.
Seeing them as obstacles to moving forward.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is said to be of real importance when we make poor decisions in life? 

 【翻译】 当我们在生活中作出糟糕的决定时，什么被认为是真正重要的？ 
 A)  预见日后可能产生的悔意。 
 B)  恰当地利用所吸取的教训。 
 C)  完善决策策略。 
 D)  把它们视为继续前进的障碍。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Making proper use of the lessons learned. 
 【定位】 P7 You will make poor decisions in life — we all do — but it's what you do with the lessons learned that matters. 
 你在人生中会做出糟糕的决定——我们都会——但真正重要的，是你如何运用从中学到的教训。 

 【信号】 but 转折 + that matters 强调 。but it's what you do with the lessons learned that matters 既有转折 but 把重点拉到后半句，又用 it's…that matters 的强调结构点出'真正要紧的'，双重信号锁定答案句。 

 【替换】 what you do with the lessons learned that matters ↔ Making proper use of the lessons learned '如何运用教训'＝'恰当运用教训' 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 A 搬来原文 there will always be a possibility for regret later 几乎整句，做成 Foreseeing the possibility for regret later.，但原文这半句只是陈述'总会有后悔的可能'，并不是 that matters 强调的'真正重要的事'，盗整句却答非所问。  借用原文：there will always be a possibility for regret later 

 C) 未提及 Perfecting the decision-making strategies. 说要'完善决策策略'，听着合理，但原文强调的是'用好已学到的教训'，并没有让你去优化决策方法，属无中生有。 
 D) 与原文相反 D 搬来原文 we can't let regret stop us from moving forward 里的 moving forward 与 obstacle 之意，做成 Seeing them as obstacles to moving forward.，但原文是'别让后悔挡住前进'，演讲者恰恰反对把决定当障碍，D 把意思反了。  借用原文：we can't let regret stop us from moving forward
